properties.name: RECURRENCE (measured on main): add_epoch still refuses a first epoch for `sequence` and `epoch_type`, in one clear round trip, on 0.76.0, 0.78.0 and main. The 0.78.0 schema door does not remove it: `--describe add_epoch` and `--list-tools` publish required ["id"] for add_epoch, add_decision, add_requirement and add_component, so the up-front reader inherits the blind spot recorded 2026-10-02
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-05, triaging art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05 (tool surface). Binaries: 0.76.0 and 0.78.0 release builds, and main at e7e304d (reports 0.78.0); scratch stores under the hub session's scratchpad, isolated HOME.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words (2026-10-01, 0.76.0): "`add_epoch` refused for a missing `sequence` (good message: next free integer is 11) — one extra round trip on every first epoch of a session."

② PRECEDENT, so this is a RECURRENCE: fact:add-epoch-create-requirements-are-published-nowhere-and-describe-schema-says-only-name-is-required-2026-10-02 measured the same on 0.77.0 and named the cost: no reader can say beforehand what CREATE needs. dec:idea-add-epoch-assigns-the-next-sequence-or-names-it is still proposed (Anthony's call on auto-assigning).

③ CANDIDATES: (a) 0.78.0's --describe closed it (it prints the full schema); (b) the schema itself does not carry create-time requirements, so every reader inherits the gap; (c) the observation is wrong.

⑤ MEASURED. `add_epoch {id, name}` on a fresh store: 0.76.0, 0.78.0 and main all exit 1 with "`sequence` is required to CREATE DesignEpoch … Also missing: epoch_type." `--describe add_epoch` on 0.78.0 and main: required ["id"], `sequence` {type integer|null, no description}, and the description never names sequence. `--list-tools` on main gives required ["id"] for add_epoch, add_decision, add_requirement and add_component. `describe_schema {node_type: DesignEpoch, required_only: true}` names only `name`. So (a) is refuted and (b) holds.

⑥ CLASS: the create-or-revise constructors enforce "required to create" in the handler, and nothing a schema reader can see carries it. Until #667 this was hidden behind the door; now the door prints the schema faithfully, and the schema is the thing that is silent.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: how many of the dual-mode constructors (22 counted on 0.77.0) still publish only ["id"]. Only these four were read on main.
